newsitem.title: USA: Jacksonville, Fla., Electric plans $150 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Jacksonville, Fla., Electric plans $150 mln bonds.

text.p: Florida's Jacksonville Electric Authority plans a water-sewer revenue refunding bond issue of $100 million to $200 million this summer, authority Treasurer Helen Kurt said Thursday.
The city of Jacksonville turned over management of its water-sewer system to the electric authority in May, and transferred debt service responsibility for water-sewer bonds to the authority.
Kurt said the refunding would come "within the next two months, hopefully sooner than that." Smith Barney Inc will be senior manager for the negotiated deal.
The agency has also included $150 million of new debt in its proposed $778 million budget for the year that begins Oct 1.
The budget still must be approved by the Jacksonville City Council.
Kurt said there had been no decision on the timing of that issue or on what form it would take.
"We may do commercial paper, some of it," she said.

Proceeds from the new money issue will fund part of a $250 million upgrade of the aging water-sewer system and improvements at treatment plants. The remaining $100 million would come from funds previously set aside for construction.

The authority's budget proposal leaves rates unchanged for the ninth straight year for both water-sewer and electric customers. Its customer base is projected to grow enough to repay the new debt without a rate hike.
The authority, which recently issued $35 million of commercial paper, has authorization to issue another $15 million of commercial paper and expects that to come by the end of 1997.
"That should take us through the end of this calendar year with out ongoing capital program," Kurt said.
